#2111. Bristol City & West Ham ticketing twist has caused a huge backlash

West Ham have enforced a major ticketing decision involving away supporters ahead of next month's home clash against Bristol City - and it's causing quite the reaction online.

Following West Ham's unprecedented relegation from the Premier League back in May, the London Stadium represents the away day for away fans throughout the Championship.

Indeed, the second-tier has never seen a larger ground than the London Stadium's 60,000-capacity, and for virtually every fanbase, an away trip to this corner of East London is one of the most notable fixtures on the calendar all season.

Fans of Bristol City, however, have just received a fresh twist that will impact their fixture away to West Ham next month, with the decision stirring up mixed reaction among supporters online.

Bristol City fans will be ticking off a major Championship away day when they travel to West Ham on December 12, though trips to Middlesbrough, West Bromwich Albion and Derby County are all on the agenda before their journey down the M4 and into East London.

But it has come with a twist that will now see a reduced number of supporters in attendance within the London Stadium away end, with West Ham having reciprocated the Robins' travelling allocation.

A ticketing announcement from the West Country outfit has confirmed this, disclosing that tickets will be on sale to supporters from next Wednesday before revealing the allocation.

Now, the Robins have informed fans that they have received an allocation of just 2,110 tickets including rail seats and general seating. This, of course, is a fairly sizeable reduction on the Hammers' typical away allocation to travelling supporters of around 3,000, yet they've simply reciprocated what City have already done.

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

The development comes following an announcement in September which revealed that Bristol City have opened the Atyeo Stand to home fans for high-profile fixtures against West Ham, Stoke and Severnside rivals Cardiff, thus reducing the number of tickes available to away supporters.

Therefore, West Ham have reacted by reducing their own allocation for the Robins faithful, and unsurprisingly, it's sparked something of a stir.

With every other Championship club to have travelled to West Ham so far this season having received a larger allocation, fans were quick to react following the Robins' announcement.

A lot of the reaction actually came from Hammers supporters, who wasted no time in lauding their club's reciprocal efforts.

This one fan, for example, applauded his side and urged them to do the same for every game against an opposing club that doesn't provide the same allocation.

Another, meanwhile, kept it direct and straight-to-the-point in response to a Bristol City punter who had questioned the allocation.

Indeed, this West Ham supporter believes the decision is evidence of the East Londoners actually getting something right, with many simply all-too-happy to see that their club has refused to simply roll over and give out the largest possible allocations while being restricted in some of their own travels on the road.

By contrast, Bristol City fans have naturally failed to share the same sentiment and believe that the Robins have been hard done by with this particular decision.

A Robins supporter here pulled no punches by describing it as an "absolute joke" - to which the Hammers' lot were, of course, swift in reminding of why the allocation has been shaved.

Emojis can sometimes tell the story, too, and in this case, they summed up exactly how another supporter of the Ashton Gate side is feeling right now.

However, another punter saw sense behind West Ham's decision and has backed the reciprocation.

There has been a split of opinion over West Ham's allocation for the travelling Bristol City contingent next month, even if many do believe that the Hammers are perfectly within their right to match the reduction.

However, there's absolutely no division when it comes to the prices that West Ham are charging for Robins fans who intend on making the trip to the London Stadium, which may just work out among their cheapest away days all season.

Adult tickets come cheaper than virtually anywhere else in the Championship at just £25, whereas 66+ and under-21 ones are even more affordable at a price of £12.

Under-18 tickets, meanwhile, will cost no more than £10, with these prices across the board paling in comparison to some other second-tier clubs.

West Ham and Bristol City fans, what do you make of this ticketing decision? Is it fair? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

All in all, then, Bristol City supporters perhaps can't complain much, and in terms of how much the fixture will cost to attend, there can be no faulting the Hammers.

That's why this fan, despite the noise, took time to praise the prices for City's trip to face Scott Parker's side away from home.

It's also no shock that one West Ham supporter - and many more silently, one can only imagine - hopes that Bristol City undertake some reciprocation of their own by charging the same prices when the promotion-chasers travel to Ashton Gate on New Year's Day.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2109. Billy Sharp sends EFL Championship promotion warning to Birmingham City

EFL legend and all-time Championship top scorer Billy Sharp has warned Birmingham City that there's still "a long way to go" after Chris Davies' side reached the second-tier summit ahead of the ongoing international break.

The Blues enjoyed an exceptional run of games between the three-week break in September and October and this current one, winning six of their seven games, three by at least a three-goal margin.

They dropped points only at Cardiff City, a side that has yet to lose at home this season, and have maintained their own unbeaten home record, winning all four games to add some gloss to a St Andrew's record which was pretty draw-heavy in the infancy of the campaign.

The win against former table-toppers Swansea City saw them climb above Middlesbrough on goal difference, and they will hold that top spot for at least another week until action resumes ahead of the Christmas period.

The question in the meantime, though, is: Can they stay there?

Billy Sharp has been a regular pundit on EFL shows this season, after formally announcing his retirement from the professional game back in October. The 40-year-old was promoted out of the Championship three times in his career, so he knows what it takes to maintain top-two form.

The all-time Championship top scorer waxed lyrical over Birmingham through the opening 15 games of the campaign, and was actually surprised that their run to the top of the table hasn't been given as much attention as it arguably should have.

FLW looks at which of the division's 24 clubs are the biggest and lowest spenders

"I think you saw glimpses last season, but they obviously didn't have that consistency," he told the Essential EFL Podcast. "They've done it really quietly, actually; no one's really spoken about them.

"He’s got the two settled centre-halves, which I've liked since last season, and I think he's playing a 4-2-3-1, which really suits him at the minute.

"He seems to have a settled side and had a little sprinkle with Millar coming in, adding a bit of magic down the left, and Stansfield got the two goals, which should do him a world of good. We know he’s got the ability, and when he’s firing, he can win games for Birmingham."

It's so far, so good for the Blues this season, but we are just 15 games in. With over two-thirds of the year still to go, and just one point separating Chris Davies' side from West Brom in fifth, Sharp feels that they can't rest on their laurels at all.

"Am I surprised they're top? I am," he admitted. "But we were saying this about Swansea on the last international break.

"It’s still tight at the top, fair play to Birmingham; going into this international break they are top, but there’s still a long way to go."

As Sharp mentioned, Birmingham's current run of six wins in seven to reach the top of the Championship has gone slightly under the radar, with the main second-tier narratives surrounding West Ham United's drop-off, or Middlesbrough struggling without Will Lankshear, for example.

Now, though, this Blues side are at the forefront of the conversation, and will be until league action resumes after the international break. Chris Davies' side are there to be shot at, and all eyes will be on whether they can handle the weight of expectation.

It's arguable that they didn't last season, with many expecting them to follow in the footsteps of Ipswich Town and make it back-to-back promotions after their record-breaking 111-point campaign in League One the year prior.

But this year, the squad is much more settled. Partnerships which were forming last year are fixed now, and there hasn't been as much squad churn as there was last summer at St Andrew's.

Plus, Chris Davies' decision to move away from a patient, heavy possession-based style has worked wonders, with the Blues packing a real punch in an attacking sense due to their desire to get the ball forward quicker.

They look a lot more ready to maintain results and handle pressure as they become the side teams want to knock off the pedestal.

Sharp also spoke about how this exact conversation was being made around Swansea's chances at promotion, with Vitor Matos' side sitting atop the Championship at the last international break.

And while the Swans did return to action with back-to-back wins, they followed that up with four defeats in five leading up to the break, including that loss at St Andrew's last time out.

They're still in contention, sitting three points off Birmingham, but the difference in performances with the pressure on, compared to when it's not, was there to be seen, and Blues have to guard against the same happening to them.

Do you think Birmingham City can maintain this promotion-winning form? Let us know in the comments.

Chris Davies' side have a tough matchup at Stoke City when play resumes, which then leads them into a run of four games against sides sitting between 18th and 22nd. A win at the bet365 Stadium would propel them into a run of, on paper, easier matches.

Perhaps, by mid-December, this could be a side with some daylight between themselves and the chasing pack, and then people may be taking their current title charge a lot more seriously.

#2108. Bradford City TV decision announced and it's causing a reaction

Bradford City fans have been left extremely frustrated by a television broadcast decision impacting their FA Cup tie against non-league Wimborne Town next month.

The Bantams have endured a dramatic opening to the new League One season, with Michael Duff recently replacing Graham Alexander as the man in the Valley Parade hotseat.

Duff has only overseen one league victory in West Yorkshire so far, but his new employers are certainly going well in cup competitions, yet to lose in the EFL Trophy whilst also making the EFL Cup quarter-finals and reaching the FA Cup second round.

Bradford comfortably dispatched Marine 7-0 on Saturday afternoon, with said victory being rewarded with a high-profile tie against Wimborne, the lowest-ranked side now left in the competition, after the Dorset club defeated League Two side Crawley Town 2-0 on Sunday.

There are, of course, plenty of former Premier League sides competing in the FA Cup's early rounds, and the likelihood of them competing against non-league sides increases the chances of television coverage.

Eight ties were selected for broadcast in the first round proper, and the same number have been chosen again for the second round between December 4th and 7th.

All 24 League One clubs have been ranked in order of size.

Bradford are one of six League One sides who will see their ties televised, with their trip to the Wyatt Homes Stadium kicking off the weekend on Friday, December 4th, with coverage beginning on TNT Sports 1 at 7PM ahead of a 7:30PM kick-off.

Other televised ties include 2021 FA Cup winners, Leicester City's trip to Dover Athletic, which now kicks off at 5:15PM on Saturday, December 5th on BBC Two.

It is approximately five hours' worth of travel from the West Yorkshire city to the town of Wimborne Minster, meaning that, at the best of times, an arduous journey would be in store for the Bradford fans.

Crawley supporters received an allocation of 500 tickets in the 3,250-capacity ground last weekend, and a similar number will be expected to make the trip to support Duff's men.

However, whilst City fans are likely to sell out such a figure, the decision to now play the game on a Friday night just three weeks before Christmas hasn't gone down well at all, with one supporter saying: "Asking people to take a day off work to go do a 10 hour round trip to Winbourne is crazy. Deserves boosted loyalty points imo."

Another said of the decision: "Friday night on the south coast. Seeing as there will only be about 200 tickets it should reduce demand."

"Did we really expect anything else - well actually the way the schedulers don't give a damn about travel times I had a feeling it might have been Monday!," one displeased City fan wrote.

"Who makes these decisions," questioned another Bantams supporter.

Bradford fans, will you be making the long journey to Wimborne for this FA Cup tie? Comment below!

Another verdict read: "Teed up perfectly for #bcafc to be on the receiving end of an FA Cup shock. Friday night, tight ground, locals right up for it, live tv....all the ingredients right there!"

"Honestly mind boggling who makes these decisions. Fair play to anyone who makes that journey on a Friday night," backed up the general feeling amongst Bradford's fanbase.

Wimborne are currently ninth in the Southern Football League Premier Division South, with four steps in the English pyramid separating themselves from Bradford.

As such, the wider public will certainly be hoping the non-league side reach the third round and potentially pluck out a 'glamour tie' involving a Premier League or high-flying Championship outfit.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Bradford, therefore, will be hoping they are not on the wrong side of a 'cupset' this time around, having been famed for such exploits in recent years during their run to the 2013 EFL Cup final and the 2014/15 FA Cup quarter-finals, where they came back from two goals down to defeat Premier League champions, Chelsea, at Stamford Bridge.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2107. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

Fernandez says: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

It remains to be seen if Chelsea land any of their three main deadline day targets with a few hours of the window to go.

Chelsea had a bid rejected for Lamine Camara, Roma have not been playing ball on Manu Kone and the identity of the mystery Premier League target has not yet emerged.

Newcastle insist the only deals they are working on for the rest of the day are the departures of Nick Woltemade on loan to Juventus and Sean Neave to Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Multiple sources deny there is any chance of Jacob Murphy leaving for Nottingham Forest despite claims of a second bid being rejected today.

High drama on Wearside where Sunderland fear their deal to sign Malick Fofana from Lyon has been hijacked by Crystal Palace.

Nobody has told Sunderland the deal is off yet, but the fact they are also lining up an alternative in the shape of Dodi Lukébakio shows they are worried.

It is understood Sunderland have made contact with Benfica this afternoon to discuss terms for Lukébakio, who is another Belgium international.

Crystal Palace are believed to have offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to Fofana which could be enough to swing things in their favour.

Manchester United are in discussions about signing the 18-year-old Leicester midfielder Louis Page. Talks ongoing with Leicester but there are no guarantees a deal will happen at this stage.

As things stand, Joshua Zirkzee seems more likely to stay at United than go. The prospects of bringing in a left-back are also fading.

Who you gon' call? ☎️ pic.twitter.com/SS0xYHtONL

West Ham are in a state of flux, trying to find their way in the Championship, and they have failed with a bid to take Michael Keane from Everton on loan. They had offers from Werder Bremen and Sevilla, too, to take Edson Álvarez out on a season-long loan. The interest from Sevilla in the Mexican was strong and the proposal would have covered all of Álvarez’s wages but West Ham were looking to recoup a significant loan fee to sanction it. That detail led to the deal falling through.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets back in the spring Matías Fernández-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target back in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernández-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment taskforce “the one”.

Moussa Diaby, the former Aston Villa winger, has put pen to paper on a second spell at Bayer Leverkusen, where he scored 49 goals in four seasons. He arrives in Germany after a two-year stint at Al-Ittihad in the Saudi Pro League.

In England, the transfer window slams shut at 11pm, but the deadline to complete deals is earlier on the Continent:

In the Scottish Premiership, deals can be completed until 5pm on Thursday, September 3.

Former Wolves, Fulham and West Ham winger Adama Traore has joined La Liga side Deportivo A Coruna.

Once one of the fastest players in the world, Traore will join forces with another speedy forward in Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to complete a vintage Premier League frontline...

Although much of the chatter today has related to Enzo Fernandez, a name that has cropped up a lot over the past hours has been that of Malick Fofana.

Sunderland had seemingly beaten Arsenal to the Lyon winger’s signature but reports have emerged that Crystal Palace are attempting to hijack Fofana’s Wearside move...

We’re still awaiting official confirmation of Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move to Tottenham Hotspur. It would mean a reunion with Roberto De Zerbi, under whom the Ukrainian played at Shakhtar Donetsk.

When asked about Mudryk in 2022, the then Brighton head coach said: “Mykhailo has the potential for a top career. In my opinion, he can also win the Ballon d’Or. He is a player of the highest level but he is also very sensitive.”

De Zerbi added: “He needs affection. We will see if he matches his potential.”

Gabriel Jesus has completed his move from Arsenal to Barcelona in a deal worth about £9m. It’s a fantastic move for the Brazilian, who had declined in importance at Arsenal after a succession of serious injuries. Arsenal would have hoped for a higher fee for a player of his reputation but his enormous salary, believed to have been worth about £250,000 a week, was always going to be problematic as they looked for buyers.

When instinct calls, you answer. ☎️ pic.twitter.com/BgZktIcJ17

The 18-year-old centre-back will become a Chelsea player in the summer of 2027, but will spend the rest of this season on loan at Selhurst Park from Atalanta.

A brief update on Jayden Danns: he is going to stay at Liverpool, rather than accept a loan in Europe. There is some significance to this as, if you had read Telegraph Sport 10 days ago, you will know that Liverpool are in a position where for the first time in 134 years, a player born within the city might not represent them. Danns is the one who can keep the record going.

Sam Johnstone is heading to Celtic ahead of a loan deal from Wolves.

The 33-year-old, capped four times by England under Gareth Southgate, is travelling to Scotland this afternoon to completed the formalities of the deal including a medical.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles has emerged as a prime target for Everton, as they look to find a solution to their right-back conundrum. The former Arsenal defender, who is now at Lyon, has been the subject of a £5m offer and the indication is that he has now taken over from Kenny Tete as the preferred option. Everton, historically, have always pushed things to the wire on transfer deadline day and this one is proving to be no different.

With Woltemade travelling to undergo a medical with Juventus for a loan move from Newcastle, that would appear to shut off one potential exit route for Joshua Zirkzee. Juventus had been looking at a season long loan for Zirkzee. Fiorentina have also been keen on Zirkzee and made an offer to United of a loan plus €30m (£25.7m) buy option but the Netherlands forward turned down the chance to go there. United would be more likely to bring in another player, probably a left-back rather than a direct replacement, if Zirkzee was to go but time running out on that front.

United had hoped to sell Manuel Ugarte and Zirkzee this summer and were in the market for buyers for Marcus Rashford, but the window could close with all three staying put. Ugarte’s serious knee injury put paid to the Uruguay midfielder leaving and Rashford has been reintergrated in the squad after Barcelona opted against taking up an option to sign him permanently.

Benfica are in talks about loaning Argentina Under-23 forward Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City, It’s likely to be a season long loan with an option to buy if finalised.

Fabio Vieira has completed his move from Arsenal to Hamburg, in a deal believed to be worth about £9m. The Portuguese midfielder has never cut it in the Premier League and it is no surprise that Arsenal have cashed in. They paid more than £30m to sign him from Porto in 2022 but he has never come close to justifying the fee. In truth, it’s one of their worst transfers under Mikel Arteta.

Southampton forward Cameron Archer is on course to sign for Auxerre on a season-long loan.

Archer has been a target for a number of Championship clubs this summer but a deal has been problematic because of his £35,000-a-week wages.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

The Argentina forward missed three training sessions last week and was not included in Diego Simeone’s squad that travelled to Sevilla last weekend.

Plenty of chatter about the future of Roma midfielder Manu Koné, who is linked with a move to Chelsea. The France international would be a strong acquisition for Xabi Alonso, but could his potential signing precede an Enzo Fernández exit? All will be revealed in due course...

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

Will Barcola hit the ground running at Anfield? The France winger registered 20 goal contributions in 49 games for Paris St-Germain last season.

A warm welcome from the skipper 😍 pic.twitter.com/95EAqUjYBn

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#2106. Notts County confirm TV decision and it's sparked backlash

Notts County's League One struggles look to be over after their four matches in a row lost in September and October, with Martin Paterson finally finding the winning formula again.

Paterson guided the Magpies back into League One earlier this year with a resounding League Two play-off final victory over Salford City, and he was backed by the Reedtz Brothers with some exciting cash signings and eye-catching loanees.

Football League World runs down their Team of the Season in League One so far this term

County were in the relegation zone of the third tier in mid-October after four defeats on the spin, but wins over Sheffield Wednesday and Mansfield Town, as well as a respectable draw at home to Stockport County, has seen the mood lift at Meadow Lane, and the pressure somewhat rise from Paterson's shoulders.

Last weekend, Notts County stepped away from league action to take part in Round One of the FA Cup, where they were handed a potential banana skin in the form of National League side Altrincham.

In-front of over 4,000 fans at Moss Lane, County went 2-1 behind to the fifth tier outfit, only for Cal Roberts to rescue the game in the 84th-minute and send it to extra time.

And despite the deteriorating foggy conditions, Notts County won out in the resulting penalty shootout, despite the lack of visibility for their supporters at the opposite end of the ground.

One of 40 clubs that were in Monday's second round draw, Notts were handed a tie against a club even further down the footballing pyramid than their previous opponents, with a trip to Northern Premier League side Guiseley on the horizon.

The West Yorkshire outfit, based around nine miles north of the city of Leeds, made it through to round two by beating Sutton United from two divisions above 1-0, and they have now been rewarded with another home clash with a much bigger outfit.

They got over 1,500 fans through the gates of Nethermoor Park last weekend, and that may be even bigger with the visit of a League One outfit, which was scheduled to take place on the weekend of December 5.

#2105. Celtic 1 Kilmarnock 0: Liam Scales scores only goal as Premiership leaders make hard work of it

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026

For Martin O’Neill, the second international break of the season should be somewhat less fretful than the first.

Seven weeks ago, with a home defeat to Ferencvaros coming in between two no-shows against Rangers, the veteran wondered aloud if it might be time to ‘wrap it up’.

O’Neill later admitted that he regretted his choice of words. He won’t, though, lament the decision to go again as he rests up in the coming days.

While the intervening weeks have often been a bumpy ride, the past four days have been a lot more like it.

Thursday’s dramatic win over Besiktas has breathed new life into Celtic’s Europa League campaign.

While by no means spectacular, this narrow victory over Kilmarnock re-established their four-point lead at the top of the Premiership and will have further dampened the sense of hysteria which was threatening to engulf the entire club.

Celtic defender Liam Scales loops the ball over Kilmarnock's goalkeeper and into the net

Scales celebrates with Camilo Duran after netting the only goal of the game at Celtic Park

Celtic striker Kasper Hogh finds the net with a crisp right-foot shot, only to have it disallowed

Celtic certainly made hard work of this. Truth be told, they should have gone into the break on the back of a far more convincing victory.

While they were right to feel wronged that Kasper Hogh saw his goalless run stretch to 16 matches after having one harshly disallowed, O’Neill’s men did not help themselves either.

Coming after Liam Scales had given them a half-time advantage, Benjamin Nygren’s missed penalty allowed Kilmarnock to keep believing right to the end.

Nonetheless, it was hard to begrudge Celtic their victory over the piece. A few weeks back, this might have been a contest in which they’d have come a cropper. They look more assured defensively than earlier in the season.

You don’t need to stay up all night researching exactly why Kilmarnock are in such peril at this stage of the season.

Neil McCann’s side began the campaign losing goals and they’ve really never stopped. They cough up more chances than any side in the top division. When it comes to shooting themselves in the foot, they’re in a league of their own.

In 13 games to date, they’ve shipped 29 goals and have kept just two clean sheets in the process. St Mirren, the side with the second worst record in the Premiership, have lost 22.

As worrying as those statistics and the Premiership table undoubtedly are, though, this felt like a step in the right direction.

In being more resolute, McCann’s men stayed in the contest right until the final whistle. They fashioned a number of decent chances throughout. There was plenty of encouragement here, even though they went down again.

For the home supporters, the much-needed positivity which had emanated from Thursday’s European win was boosted by the return to the starting line-up of Jota for the first time since April 2025.

Notably, only three out of nine of Celtic’s summer signings made the squad, with Sam Johnstone the only one involved who arrived on deadline day.

O’Neill was indebted to the on-loan Wolves man inside the first minute. Ieuan Owen skipped away from Callum McGregor then Colby Donovan down the left and put in a dangerous cross. Twice Tom Lowery hit the target. Twice the Celtic keeper stood up tall.

Lowery immediately had his name taken by John Beaton for a clumsy foul on Nygren.

Despite their precarious position, to their credit, Kilmarnock didn’t come to Parkhead just to defend. Tyreece John-Jules, their main striker, had an abundance of support in the form of Owen, Greg Kiltie and Joe Hugill.

Between them, they fashioned enough half chances. They just didn’t have ice in the veins at the right moments.

Hogh was right to feel aggrieved at the decision which cost him that elusive goal. Truthfully, there was very little in Mika Baur’s challenge on Kiltie which was retrospectively penalised.

Duran gathered and fed Nygren. The Swede swivelled and rolled the ball into Hogh’s path. A crisp right-foot finish was not that of a player lacking in confidence.

The Dane’s lengthy celebrations included a look up to the heavens. By the time Beaton made his way to the monitor and chalked the goal off, Hogh could have been forgiven for feeling that someone up there had it in for him.

To Hogh’s credit, he didn’t let it affect him. Moments later, after being played in by Duran, he was only denied his revenge by the outstretched leg of Nico Mantl.

Hogh then played Duran in with a clever back-heel. The Colombian lashed his effort just wide.

Celtic’s pressure was mounting and they edged in front on 26 minutes with Duran, yet again excellent throughout, the architect.

His clipped cross from the right caught the Kilmarnock defence flat-footed. Scales extended his left foot and watched the ball rise to the point where it appeared to be going over.

With Mantl hoping that it would clear his bar, it looped into the net. There was no disputing this one.

Required to take more risks, Killie had to be careful when they turned the ball over. Hugill and Cathal McCarthy were both booked for crude fouls on Duran and Jota, respectively.

While Celtic began to control the affair, the visitors were not without their moments. Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s stinging strike from 25 yards forced Johnstone into another solid stop.

While Jota looked good in moments, it’s clearly going to take some time before he’s fully up to speed. The same might apply to Hyun-jun Yang, the man who replaced him at the interval, after being sidelined for six weeks with a hamstring injury.

Donovan came close to wrapping up the three points with an enterprising run and shot with his left foot which flew just wide.

Duran’s close control and speed across the ground bought him a yard for a shot. Having seen it late, Mantl dealt with it well.

Hogh actually performed well here. He was tidy with the ball and frequently brought team-mates into play. He just didn’t hit the target often enough. That again cost him when he spun neatly in the box and tried his luck midway through the second period.

You couldn’t fault him when he seized on Kieran Tierney’s cross, though. The saving block from Killie substitute MJ Kamson-Kamara was tremendous.

With the home supporters longing for a clinching second goal, Duran dumped a shot into the side netting before the industrious Baur was flagged offside after firing home.

The wait would go on. Initially adjudged to have struck Aaron Tshibola’s arm just outside the box, Yang’s strike would earn Celtic a spot-kick with 14 minutes remaining after a VAR review.

Nygren just never looked confident as he spotted the ball. Mantl dived to his right and made a comfortable save. Those hoping for a sharp exit sat back in their seats.

The sight of Baur hobbling badly after being caught by Tshibola didn’t make the viewing in the final moments any easier. All that truly counted for the home fans, though, was that Celtic got over the line.

#2104. 6 EFL clubs who must eye £0 Wilfried Zaha transfer

Championship clubs will already have one eye on the January transfer window as they look to strengthen their squads, even if there is a lot of football to be played between now and the New Year.

Another problem facing clubs trying to do deals in January is the reluctance of rivals to sell players halfway through the season.

It’s obvious why that is the case, so deals in the winter window often come at a premium, which makes business harder to do.

However, one market clubs could explore is the free agent one, as there are still some talented individuals who are without a club.

Wilfried Zaha certainly falls into that category, with the Crystal Palace legend yet to return to the game since his Galatasaray contract expired in the summer.

The forward last played on loan at Charlotte FC in May, so he would take time to get up to speed, but, even at 34, you still get the feeling Zaha could contribute a lot.

Football League World looks at the average attendance table in the Championship so far this season

The Ivory Coast international had been linked with a move to Lazio last month, but nothing materialised, and, given his age, he may want to get back playing in the UK, where he has spent most of his life.

With that in mind, we look at SIX EFL clubs who should consider a move for Zaha…

Wrexham have signed several big-names in their journey from non-league to the Championship, and Zaha could help them take that next step to the Premier League.

His profile would make this an intriguing signing, but, more importantly, he would beef up Phil Parkinson’s squad, which is lacking in the final third. The likes of Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead and Sam Smith have suffered injuries, with the latter ruled out for the season.

So, in January, Wrexham are widely expected to bring in at least one attacker, but they could still benefit from Zaha as well, who could play in the three attacking roles in Parkinson’s XI, and he would provide the team with some much-needed pace and spark.

Birmingham are another ambitious club at this level, and they will feel that promotion to the Premier League is a very real possibility considering they sit top of the league right now.

But, the one concern for Chris Davies will centre on the squad depth, as the lack of quality behind their best XI is a worry. So, adding a player like Zaha would make a lot of sense, as he could provide quality cover down both flanks.

Given his pedigree, Zaha would back himself to force his way into the best XI, and his experience and know-how could be just what Blues need to get over the line this season.

As mentioned, Zaha has spent most of his life in London, so, he would surely be open to playing in the capital once again, and West Ham would be a good fit.

After a positive start, Manor Solomon’s form has dipped, and with Edvin Austbo and Jarrod Bowen also at the club, you could argue the Hammers are one winger short, so Zaha could add to the squad for this season at least.

Where do West Ham need to strengthen in January? Let us know in the comments below.

This campaign is all about promotion for West Ham, so a short-term solution can’t be dismissed, and if Zaha helps the Irons back to the top flight, it would be the perfect outcome for all parties.

Following on from that, if Zaha wants a London club that offers a more realistic route to the first-team, then QPR could appeal, and they would benefit from the attacker in the squad.

Julien Stephan’s side will also fancy their chances of winning promotion, but there will be concerns if they have the squad and the experience to cope with the demands of the Championship.

So, Zaha would help on both fronts, and he is the sort of unpredictable, skilful player that the R’s fans enjoy watching.

If first-team football is the priority, then Zaha may have to lower his standards, but he would walk into many mid-table Championship sides, including Sheffield United.

Chris Wilder doesn’t have the biggest budget to work with at this level, so he will have his eye on free agents, and he would surely back himself to get Zaha back enjoying his football, which would make him a huge asset at this level.

However, if the ex-Lyon man wants regular football, he knows he would get it at Pride Park, and, at this stage of his career, that may be something that Zaha decides to prioritise.

#2103. Crystal Palace twist hands major boost to Steve Gibson and Middlesbrough

It has been an outstanding start to the season for Middlesbrough in the Championship.

After losing to Hull City in last season's play-off final, Middlesbrough have started strongly as they look to bounce back from their Wembley heartbreak, and head coach Kim Hellberg has earned plenty of admirers for his work at the Riverside Stadium this campaign.

Middlesbrough spent big in the transfer window this summer as they look to finally secure a long-awaited return to the Premier League, and striker Will Lankshear was the club's marquee signing as he joined from Tottenham Hotspur for an initial fee of around £10 million, plus a further £10 million in add-ons.

Lankshear was not the only headline addition of the summer for Boro, with the likes of Radek Vitek, Ashley Phillips, Max Arfsten, Sebastian Berhalter, Rokas Pukstas and Kyle Joseph also arriving for significant transfer fees, and the club's ambitious squad rebuild has certainly had the desired effect so far.

It was a disappointing week for Boro before the international break as they picked up just one point from two away games at Wrexham and Watford, but while they were knocked off top spot on goal difference by Birmingham City, they currently sit second in the Championship table.

However, it seems Boro's impressive form has had some unwanted consequences for the Teesside outfit, with reports emerging over the weekend claiming that Hellberg was on the radar of top flight side Crystal Palace as they prepared to part company with Pierre Sage.

Hellberg was not the only name linked with Crystal Palace, with Thomas Frank, Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Vitor Pereira, Vitor Matos, Tony Popovic, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner also believed to have been under consideration.

After a poor start to the season that has left them bottom of the Premier League table, the Eagles confirmed Sage's departure on Thursday after just 16 games in charge, but while Middlesbrough may have feared that the Frenchman's exit would lead to an approach for Hellberg, it seems that will not be the case.

Frank was understood to be the leading contender to replace Sage, and Palace are now reportedly in advanced talks with the former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur boss about taking over at Selhurst Park, albeit a deal has not yet been finalised.

Given that Frank is out of work and has Premier League experience under his belt, it is easy to see why the Eagles have opted for the Dane in their current predicament, but the fact that Hellberg's name was mentioned shows that his reputation in English football is growing.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Having lost Rob Edwards to Wolverhampton Wanderers just before the November international break last season, Middlesbrough owner Steve Gibson could have been forgiven for fearing the worst when the speculation arose linking Hellberg with Crystal Palace.

In an eerie similarity to the present situation, Boro were also second in the Championship table last November when Edwards made the controversial decision to swap the Riverside Stadium for Molineux after just 16 games in charge, but it appears that history will not be repeating itself.

While Edwards was widely criticised for his response when quizzed about the Wolves job prior to his eventual departure, infamously stating that his daughter had informed him of the rumours when they first surfaced, Hellberg immediately dismissed any talk about him making the switch to Selhurst Park and insisted that he remained fully committed to Boro.

Earlier this week, when asked by Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen how he felt about the Palace reports, Hellberg replied: "Absolutely nothing, absolutely nothing.

"It's always nice to be on lists like that, if that's the case — it shows you've done something right. But I think it's mostly just talk, and, for me, it's all about doing a good job here.

"We actually have a chance to get promoted this year. We feel that there is a chance, but then it's clear that it will be difficult.

"We are one of five, six teams, maybe not the biggest favourites, but, behind them, I think we have a good chance.

"My focus is here and hopefully we can get up, that would have been fantastic of course."

While Hellberg's loyalty to Boro has ultimately not been tested by any formal approach from the Eagles, it is clear that the 38-year-old's head has not been turned by the gossip about his future, and his comments will be music to Gibson's ears after his frustrating experience with Edwards.

Hellberg has become a hugely popular figure on Teesside over the past year, and he is regarded as one of the most exciting managers outside the Premier League, having built a team that plays an attractive, attacking brand of football, even if Boro have been a little vulnerable defensively at times this season.

Should Kim Hellberg leave Middlesbrough if a Premier League club comes calling this season? Tell us in the comments below!

Further interest in Hellberg is inevitable over the coming months if Boro continue on their current trajectory, but Gibson will be incredibly relieved to have held on to his highly-rated coach for now at least.

#2101. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2100. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”
