#1988. Man United are a rotten, shambolic mess. They lack intelligence, look uncoached and fumbling, failing Michael Carrick is not the man to arrest this trauma, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 14:32 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 20:25 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United do not have a football team, more a collection of adrenaline junkies. Over time, it will not be enough.

So deficient are Michael Carrick's players that they surely can't keep their manager in a job for much longer. For the most part United are shambolic, a mess. At times they play football so devoid of intelligence and competence that it's almost impossible to fathom. They look uncoached.

Yet here they were for the second night running at Old Trafford, completing a lap of honour at full-time while their supporters sang the name of Carrick as he completed his own journey in front of the Stretford End towards the tunnel.

United – it's worth pointing out – are third bottom of the Premier League. They haven't won in the league since August and have conceded more goals across all competitions – 30 – than any team bar Crystal Palace in Europe's top divisions.

But at Old Trafford they will cling to anything to help them look in the mirror without laughing and currently the currency is comebacks. There was one against Roma in the Champions League last Tuesday and here – quite remarkably – there were two in one game.

None of it should really mean anything in the grand scheme. United are rotten, capable of playing effectively only when something gives them an energy spike with which to roll. It makes for quite hypnotic theatre but has inadequacy and desperation at its core.

Patrick Dorgu (centre) scored a late equaliser as troubled Man United drew 4-4 vs Aston Villa

Dorgu scored in the 96th-minute with this header but United sit 18th in the Premier League

Despite the draw, Michael Carrick's position as United head coach looks increasingly doubtful

It won't sustain them or indeed their fumbling, failing manager. But for the moment it's what they have and what they are.

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Mazraoui 4, Yoro 6, Maguire 5 (Heaven 46, 5), Dalot 3 (Dorgu 66, 8); Tielemans 6 (Mount 66, 5), Mainoo 6; Amad 5 (Lacey 66, 7), Fernandes 6, Cunha 7; Mbeumo 5 (Zirkzee 83, 7)

Goals: Fernandes (16 pen), Tielemans (44), Zirkzee (90+2), Dorgu (90+6)

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 5, Lindelof 6, Torres 6, Maatsen 4; Goretzka 6 (Mbaye 78, 6), Kamara 4; Alysson 7 (Barkley 71, 6), McGinn 8 (Hemmings 71, 6), Manzambi 6; Jackson 6 (Madjo 86)

Goals: Alysson (1), Jackson (4), McGinn (48 pen), Goretzka (53)

Here, they twice trailed by two, at the start of both halves. They were 2-0 down after only four minutes and 4-2 behind after 53. Somehow they managed not to lose.

The two goals United scored in added time at the end of the game came from absolutely nowhere. On the touchline Carrick – free from total humiliation for the second time in six days – raised a single finger to the sky.

In the directors' box – where the TV companies seem to have a camera permanently trained these days – fist pumps were in evidence from those in United blazers.

This was another uncomfortable afternoon for Messrs Ratcliffe, Wilcox and Berrada. A collection of new banners in the crowd made feelings known.

For now, Carrick is being spared any of the blame. That is strange and wrong but tells us much about the confused nature of the modern United. If they blame one of their own then they really do have nowhere left to go in search of self-respect.

United's opening against Roma last week had been traumatic enough. This was even worse but the root of it was desperately familiar – incompetent football.

The hapless United full-back Diogo Dalot was to blame for the first goal as Villa's Brazilian Alysson blasted his shot through the Portuguese's limp challenge. Later – after conceding a second half penalty – Dalot was booed off by his own fans.

That was painful and unedifying but completely understandable. Dalot has played more than 250 games for United yet has never even been good enough.

Aston Villa took the lead after just 59 seconds when Alysson (centre) scored at Old Trafford

Nicolas Jackson (centre) doubled the visitors' lead on four minutes as they made a dream start

Bruno Fernandes pulled one back for the hosts with a penalty on 16 minutes in a crazy start

For goal two, goalkeeper Senne Lammens was culpable as he pushed Alysson's shot into the path of Nicolas Jackson.

Once again United were in sink or swim territory. Once again, amazingly, they kept their heads above water – at least for a while.

Boubacar Kamara's 13th minute challenge on Matheus Cunha was stupid as the Brazilian was heading away from goal. But the Bruno Fernandes penalty that followed was calm and precise and the shot of belief United needed was theirs.

For the next 20 minutes or so, Carrick's team played well off the back of it. It was the only part of their game that will look good on the highlights. The United front four pressed and harried the Villa defence to the extent that Unai Emery's team couldn't get up the field.

Villa keeper Zion Suzuki saved well from a Cunha curler while subsequent shots from Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Amad Diallo took deflections and narrowly missed the target.

At some stage it felt as though United's energy must drop. Over time it did. But then they equalised.

Moments after seeing Suzuki save one of his own efforts, Amad found space to pull the ball back for Youri Tielemans who placed his first United goal in from 18 yards against his old club. Carrick's team deserved to be level at that stage and had played some enterprising football to get there. But their self-harm gene surfaced again before long.

Youri Tielemans (right) brought United level before half-time with this strike vs his old club

John McGinn put Villa ahead again just minutes after half-time from the penalty spot

Leon Goretkza (left) made it 4-2 to Villa with this close-range strike as they looked set to win

Joshua Zirkzee (left) pulled one back in second-half stoppage-time with this finish for United

Alysson had almost scored with the last big moment of the first half and in the 47th minute he drew an utterly dumb foul from Dalot and John McGinn scored the penalty firmly.

United are beyond compare in the Premier League when it comes to this kind of thing. Who else in the top flight concedes the kind of goals they do? A case in point came in the 53rd minute.

McGinn's free-kick was heading across goal and away when United defender Leny Yoro inexplicably headed it towards his own goal. Lammens somehow touched the ball on to the bar but when it dropped Leon Goretzka poked it in.

That was the 16th goal United had conceded in the last five games and this time the attempt at a fightback was more muted.

There were some half chances – shots from Cunha and Fernandes – and some territory in which to play.

But this was a game Villa were now able to control rather better and they looked set to ease home until Patrick Dorgu crossed for Joshua Zirkzee to ease a goal in from out of nothing in the 2nd minute of added time.

Old Trafford was emptying fast by the time Dorgu headed in a 96th equaliser from a corner. But by then the collective blood was up once more and it was enough.

Villa appealed for a foul on goalkeeper Suzuki and it's true Lammens had gone looking for him. Was the contact between the two 'keepers significant enough to warrant VAR intervention? Probably not. United had their draw and they had a point.

If the season ended today, they would be down. Yet they were cheered off. Some things you just can't make up.

#1986. ‘Right now…’ – Liverpool-linked Premier League star makes his plans clear amid transfer rumours

One Premier League player who’s reportedly being targeted by Liverpool has issued a reponse to the transfer speculation surrounding him.

Earlier this week, TEAMtalk claimed that Anfield chiefs are eyeing Bart Verbruggen as a potential long-term successor to Alisson Becker, who’s now 34 and – as it stands – will be out of contract in seven months’ time.

The Brighton goalkeeper was reportedly among a shortlist of candidates being considered by the Reds prior to the summer transfer window, with the Merseysiders eventually agreeing a deal to sign Lucca Brughmans, who’ll join from Genk next summer.

Verbruggen – who’s currently with the Netherlands squad for their concluding UEFA Nations League fixtures – has insisted that despite the rumoured interest from Liverpool, he’s more than happy with the Seagulls, who currently sit second in the Premier League.

The 24-year-old said (via NOS): “Right now we’re doing really well at Brighton, so it would be a real shame to ruin that by living in the future. I really try to stay in the moment, to focus on what is currently going on. I enjoy that, and that is also how I perform best.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Brighton’s magnificent season so far has been underpinned by the excellence of the man between the sticks, who’s kept seven clean sheets in 10 league games and conceded just three times in eight top-flight matches since a 4-3 defeat at Chelsea in August (Transfermarkt).

Figures from Fotmob show that he’s prevented 4.39 xG worth of goals for his team, more than anyone else in the Premier League, and he put in a heroic display in the Seagulls’ recent win at Manchester City as he recorded no fewer than seven saves (Sky Sports).

Those performance levels would indicate that he’d be an ideal successor to Alisson, although there’s been renewed hope in recent days that Liverpool’s number 1 could extend his contract for another year or two, with his agent currently in talks with the club to that effect.

Giorgi Mamardashvili was signed with the intention of succeeding the Brazilian eventually, although the 26-year-old hasn’t always convinced during his time with the Reds so far, and Brughmans will add to the queue once he joins ahead of next season.

Right now there wouldn’t seem to be any urgent need for LFC to move heaven and earth to sign Verbruggen, but if circumstances were to change regarding their current goalkeeping options, it could be worth keeping a hand in should the opportunity arise to move for the Brighton stopper.

#1984. Why West Ham’s Fulham Defeat Gives Scott Parker Plenty To Be Pleased About

West Ham United were beaten 1-0 by Fulham in a behind-closed-doors friendly on Thursday, but I don’t think the result matters at all. If anything, losing by just one goal to Premier League opposition when we’ve got ten players missing on international duty is no shame whatsoever.

According to ExWHUEmployee, reporting through The West Ham Way, the match was arranged to give Scott Parker an opportunity to assess some of his players and help others build up their match fitness. No team sheet has been made public, so we don’t know exactly who featured.

What I’m particularly impressed by is how quickly Parker has organised and sorted this out. He’s barely been in the job five minutes, yet he’s already managed to arrange a friendly against Premier League opposition, presumably using his Fulham connections to get it done. That’s exactly the sort of proactive approach needed to drag the club back up the league table.

The bit I found particularly interesting was the emphasis on getting players up to fitness.

From that point of view, I’d have thought Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez would be prime candidates to have participated in the game. Alphonse Areola would also be an obvious beneficiary if he’s recovered sufficiently from his recent injury.

It’s also important for Parker to have a look at some of the other academy goalkeepers, particularly given the concerns over Fin Herrick’s fitness and the recent poor form of Mads Hermansen.

I’d rather hope Lewis Orford played some part in the game as well. He’s not getting nearly enough first-team football, and this would have been an ideal opportunity to show the new manager what he can do.

And, as I wrote earlier this week, the international break is going to afford Pablo the opportunity to try to impress the new Hammers manager.

Parker omitted the Brazilian striker from his first two matchday squads altogether, so a friendly like this could have been particularly useful for him.

We already knew that Parker’s preparations would be disrupted by the international call-ups, but he’s clearly not prepared to sit around waiting for everybody to return.

He’s taken a situation where ten players are unavailable and turned it into an opportunity to assess the rest of his squad against decent opposition.

I wouldn’t be remotely concerned about the 1-0 defeat. We don’t know who played, how many substitutions were made or even whether Parker was particularly interested in winning the match. Hopefully those details will be revealed by Ex later today?

For all we know, he may have learnt more from this game than he would have from a comfortable victory against weaker opposition.

It’s a thumbs up from me for Parker being proactive, particularly so early in his West Ham managerial career.

The only question is whether he’ll arrange another friendly next week before the Championship resumes against Preston.

#1983. West Ham-Linked Rangers Giant Features In Spain Victory

West Ham United transfer target Ryan Naderi was handed a starting place for Czechia against Spain in Thursday night’s UEFA Nations League encounter, which ended in a 2-0 victory for the Spanish.

The 6ft 4in Rangers striker, who has recently been linked with a January move to West Ham, played 66 minutes before being substituted. Spain took the lead through an Álex Baena penalty in the 39th minute, with Marc Pubill adding a second deep into stoppage time.

There was another West Ham connection to the match, with Tomáš Souček returning to international action as an 85th-minute substitute as Marin covered earlier today. Former Hammers Vladimír Coufal and Alex Král were also in the Czech starting line-up.

That sets up a particularly interesting encounter with England at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on Sunday evening. The three lions spluttered to a 2-1 victory against Slaven Bilic’s Croatia last with Harry Kane scoring the winner from the spot.

The two sides are competing for top spot in Group A3, with the match kicking off at 7.45pm GMT.

Meanwhile, from a West Ham perspective, it is encouraging to see Souček back on the pitch following his recent injury problems, even if his involvement was limited to the closing stages.

#1982. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1981. Shrewd appointments usher in new era of reconciliation | West Ham News

Very slowly, with each new hire, be it high profile such as a head coach, or a less visible appointment behind the scenes, West Ham United is travelling in a new direction. The combative era of Sullivan and Brady calling supporters their ‘customers’ and riding roughshod over fan opinions seems well and truly in the past.

Their new hire – head of supporter services and fan engagement (she’ll never get that job title on a business card) Arsenal’s Khali Parsons is a sign of the direction of travel as the Club attempts to heal ten years plus of division between owners and supporters that has been a corrosive backdrop to the football club’s history since before the move from Upton Park.

Nothing, of course, can change the hugely unpopular sale of the old ground and the dissatisfaction over the ‘rented home’ which the club now occupy, but there does appear to have been some serious ‘listening’ going on rather than the scant lip service paid to supporters’ grievances by Karren Brady in the bad old days.

According to westhamworld.co.uk“Parsons will officially take up the role in January 2027 and will also become the club co-chair of West Ham’s Fan Advisory Board, replacing Paul Stringer, [Chief Marketing and Media officer] who is filling the position on an interim basis….Her arrival comes at an important time for West Ham, with the club’s senior leadership structure changing significantly and supporter trust one of the issues the new hierarchy has openly acknowledged needs rebuilding.”

Cult Hero Martin in his playing days at West Ham – now goal keeping coach for u21’s

Indeed, the news also that former Hammer David Martin is to return to the club as u21 goal keeping coach could be seen as further news of a return to a club better in touch with, and more comfortable with it’s own heritage.

Not quite sure how it will feel as a West Ham fan, all of this unity after so many years of protest. Heaven help us if we also start winning games again: We really will have to pinch ourselves.

#1980. Premier League star's miscarriage heartbreak: Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz reveals off-field agony in emotional interview - before sharing his wife is pregnant again

Published: 06:24 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 04:12 EST, 9 November 2026

Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz has opened up on his 'really difficult' off-field issues, with the Brazilian revealing he and his wife suffered a miscarriage last year.

Muniz, 25, earned the Cottagers a point in Saturday's draw against Newcastle, with his 83rd minute strike his first Premier League goal since August 2025.

The centre forward, speaking with club media after the Craven Cottage game, spoke candidly of the difficulties he has faced with wife Jady - who are now expecting again after a turbulent year.

'Last season was really difficult for me because, now I can say, I had surgery, my wife was pregnant last season but unfortunately we lost the baby,' he said.

'But God is good all the time and now she is pregnant again. The goal was for my baby and I hope this season will be different to last season.'

Fulham star Rodrigo Muniz opened up on his personal agony after scoring on Saturday

Muniz revealed his wife Jady suffered a miscarriage but they are now pregnant again

Muniz has not been afforded a start by new Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, making all eight of his Premier League appearances off the bench so far this season.

He hopes that his contribution against the Toon has done enough to earn his manager's trust after the international break.

'I train hard every week to get opportunities to play and I want to play more,' he said.

'I cannot control that but I showed to the gaffer I want to play more.

'And I have to keep training hard for him to say, 'okay, now is your time', and then I'm ready.

'To be a striker, you need to be ready to play five or ten minutes. Of course, I want to play more. And I want to start as well.

'We have a lot of players in the national team. We train with, I think, ten players.

'It's really important because we cannot stay out for too long.

'And when we have time to work it's really good – because it's really important that the gaffer can show us what he wants and we have time to do it.'

#1979. Joe Hart pinpoints ‘unbelievable’ Alisson Becker trait which makes him ‘one of the best’

Joe Hart has proclaimed that Alisson Becker will ‘forever be regarded as one of the best’ goalkeepers to have graced the Premier League.

Liverpool’s number 1 has been rightly acknowledged as one of the foremost players in his position in world football since his move to Anfield in 2018 and has been pivotal towards the trophies won by the Reds in that time.

He produced one of his greatest LFC performances in the victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, with his tally of six saves including a world-class reaction stop from Daichi Kamada which left the Eagles attacker astounded.

In an interview with The Athletic, Hart lavished praise on Alisson for the consistency he’s shown throughout his time in England, and especially his prowess in one-on-saves.

The ex-Manchester City stopper said of the 34-year-old: “One of the best to do it in the Premier League. What I love is his simplicity. He’s not necessarily eye-catching in the way he moves, but it’s the way he deals with everything.

“He makes massive saves. His one-on-one technique is unbelievable, and he has made it his own. He very rarely gets beaten one-on-one, which in this Premier League is incredible because you’re up against some of the best strikers in the world.

“He’s struggled a bit with injuries lately, but I think he’ll forever be regarded as one of the best to play the position.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Last weekend, Alisson produced a perfect example of the one-on-one ability that Hart pinpointed by thwarting Yeremy Pino when the Crystal Palace forward was through on goal, a significant intervention at a time that Liverpool were 2-0 up.

When it comes to ‘massive saves’, it mightn’t quite be in the same category as his legendary stoppage-time heroics against Napoli in December 2018 when our Champions League campaign was in the balance, but it showed that the 34-year-old remains a world-class goalkeeper.

His outstanding display at Selhurst Park came after a couple of costly misjudgements in defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, which shows the Brazilian’s strength of character to put those unfortunate moments behind him and come up trumps for his team.

Alisson’s agent Ze Maria revealed in recent days that talks have begun over a prospective contract renewal at Liverpool, with the Reds’ number 1 having said after the win at Palace that he’d like to stay at Anfield beyond the expiry of his current deal next summer.

More heroics like those he produced in south London four days ago, and an extension to his existing terms should be a no-brainer for sporting director Julian Ward.

#1978. West Ham Ticket Row: A Bit Of Pettiness? I’m All For It

West Ham United’s ticketing arrangements for the forthcoming Championship clash with Bristol City have caused controversy, but I have to say I’m firmly on the Hammers’ side with this one. If there’s an element of tit for tat involved, I don’t have a problem with it at all.

Bristol City supporters might not particularly like the situation, but there is some history between the two clubs when it comes to ticket allocations. During the FA Cup meeting in January 2024, Bristol City took their full allocation of around 9,000 tickets at the London Stadium, resulting in thousands of West Ham season-ticket holders having to move from their usual seats.

That caused considerable frustration at the time, with the West Ham United Supporters’ Trust seeking clarification from the club over the arrangements. So if the current situation feels like a bit of payback, I can certainly understand why.

One thing West Ham’s relegation to the Championship has provided is a real reality check when it comes to the treatment of travelling supporters.

In the Premier League, there was at least some collective understanding that away supporters shouldn’t be completely fleeced. The Football Supporters’ Federation’s original Twenty’s Plenty campaign eventually helped bring about the £30 away-ticket cap, which has remained in place since 2016.

It wasn’t perfect, and £30 was still more than supporters had originally campaigned for, but at least there was a limit.

That protection doesn’t exist across the Championship, and we’re now seeing the difference.

Take West Ham’s trip to Birmingham City in December, for example. According to the club’s official ticket information, adult supporters will be charged £37.50 for the privilege of watching the Hammers at St Andrew’s.

And it definitely feels like Championship clubs are treating us like absolute mugs.

When West Ham roll into town, we’re seen as a cash cow. Clubs know we’re going to bring a substantial travelling support, and it increasingly feels as though they’re happy to make the most of it.

Of course, I understand that Championship clubs have their own financial pressures, but that doesn’t make it any easier for supporters who are already spending a fortune travelling around the country.

I don’t have a problem with West Ham looking after our own fans, even if that means upsetting a few visiting supporters along the way.

Perhaps there’s a little bit of pettiness involved, but realistically, I don’t mind that either.

We’re West Ham, and the club should be looking after our fans. That ought to be the priority, particularly when supporters have been asked to put up with so much since dropping into the Championship.

And any Bristol City fans who don’t like it probably should look at their own club’s conduct when we played them in the FA Cup.

I don’t particularly want to see football clubs getting into an endless argument over ticket allocations, and ultimately I’d prefer supporters everywhere to be treated fairly.

But when it comes to this particular situation, I’m not going to criticise the West Ham hierarchy for giving a bit back.

Sometimes tit for tat is exactly what it looks like, and on this occasion, I’m perfectly happy with it.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Gonzo, I dont think at any point actually say what the club has done. You dont appear to explain what the pettiness is around, or even what it is we are doing? You said I’m not going to criticise the West Ham hierarchy for giving a bit back. So what bit is it they are giving back? You have gone all round the houses with everything else, but left the part about how the club is getting its own back completely void of details….so if Bristol City dont like it….like what exactly? lol

Wow i didn’t realise away supporters weren’t getting the sane compulsory pricing in the Champs, I used to love away games much better atmosphere and experience.

Next season if we don’t go up which is a possibility the chairman should speak to all the other clubs and arrange a reciprocal agreement, we will charge your fans what you charge ours.

#1976. Liverpool could replicate Jeremy Jacquet masterclass with move for ‘super’ teenage prospect

With Jeremy Jacquet already looking like a masterstroke of a signing, Liverpool could seek to replicate that coup with another transfer which’d bear strong echoes of the Frenchman’s arrival.

The right-back position at Anfield has been a volatile one since Trent Alexander-Arnold’s exit 18 months ago, with Conor Bradley sidelined by a serious knee injury and Jeremie Frimpong failing to truly convince since he joined in the summer of 2025 (whilst also suffering several injuries of his own).

It’s led to Andoni Iraola deploying the on-loan Ronald Araujo – conventionally a centre-back – on the right-hand side of defence, and thankfully the Uruguayan has been a sturdy presence in the Reds’ back four so far this season.

Nearly a year on from agreeing a deal to sign Jacquet, Liverpool could once more turn to Ligue 1 for a breakthrough defensive prospect.

According to Get French Football News, the Reds are currently monitoring Le Havre right-back Djibril Ouziad, who’s also being watched by Aston Villa.

The 17-year-old signed his first professional contract at the Stade Oceane in September, penning terms until 2030, but he’s deemed ‘likely to leave’ next summer even if his current club pull themselves out of the relegation zone in the French top flight.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Similar to how Jacquet properly established himself in Rennes’ first team last season, Ouziad is doing likewise with Le Havre this term, starting all but two of their league games so far in 2026/27 and making the right-back berth his own since being handed his senior debut in August.

A data analysis from Spencer Mossman highlighted the teenager as a ‘super creator’ who provides a serious threat from crosses and also marked him out as a ‘productive dribbler’ who’s likely to be ‘on a lot of radars very soon’.

The 17-year-old has been a rare plus point in a hithero miserable campaign for the Normandy outfit, and the creative influence that he provides from right-back seems reminiscent of Alexander-Arnold in his pomp at Liverpool.

What happens with Araujo’s future may well have a big bearing on whether or not the Reds go all-out to try and sign Ouziad. If the Uruguayan turns his loan move into a permanent transfer, there would be no great need for right-sided defensive reinforcements at Anfield.

However, if he goes back to Barcelona next summer and Frimpong were to depart amid rumours of Saudi Arabian interest, then Julian Ward might push hard in his attempts to snap up the Le Havre starlet.

#1975. Celtic fans disgracefully boo during minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday: Referee ends tribute after just 13 SECONDS - even after warning from the PA announcer

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:28 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:51 EST, 9 November 2026

Celtic were forced to curtail plans to commemorate Remembrance Day after a section of their supporters booed during the planned minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The Bhoys hosted Kilmarnock in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday - with Liam Scales' goal proving the difference in a 1-0 win.

However, ahead of kick-off at Parkhead, the annual tribute to the armed forces and their families was overshadowed by some fans' loud jeers.

As the players from both teams gathered around the centre-circle, an announcement on the public address system said: 'We will have a minute's silence today on Remembrance Sunday to remember all victims of all conflicts. We remember, in particular, the men who served Celtic football club and lost their lives at wartime.'

The audible disdain resulted in referee John Beaton being forced to cut the silence after just 13 seconds.

The noise was so palpable that the Celtic TV broadcast turned down the volume to try and minimise its impact too.

The minute's silence ahead of Celtic versus Kilmarnock was cut short due to some fans booing

Celtic TV turned down the volume to try and minimise the jeers during the curtailed silence

Referee John Beaton (right) cut the minute's silence after 13 seconds as a result of the booing

Furthermore, the lower tier of the standing section was empty until the Green Brigade and other fans started to file in from the concourse when referee Beaton’s whistle signalled the end of the tribute.

Football clubs across the United Kingdom observe a minute's silence with their nearest home fixture around Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day - with the latter on November 11.

Many teams also wear poppies, something Kilmarnock wore on their strip, but Celtic didn't.

Some Celtic supporters refuse to partake in the tradition or actively take a stance against it, often citing the club’s Irish roots and linking it to the British Army‘s role in The Troubles.

Last season, in a quirk, Celtic hosted Kilmarnock on Remembrance Sunday too - with that minute's silence also cut short due to jeering. That time referee Don Robertson cut it short at 15 seconds.

As well as the booing in that match last term, some fans turned their back on the minute's silence and also made gestures.

Sunday's 1-0 win over Kilmarnock sees Celtic regain their four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership.

It was under-pressure Martin O'Neill's side's first league win in their last three games.

Scales scored the only goal of the game on 26 minutes when he hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner.

Celtic fans show their displeasure during the minute's silence for Remembrance Day in 2025

Celtic - and Kasper Hogh in particular - otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

Celtic have 31 points from their opening 13 matches - four more than bitter rivals Rangers who sit second but have a game in hand.

Kilmarnock remain rooted to the bottom of the table with nine points from 13 games - two adrift of 11th-place Aberdeen who have played a match fewer.

#1974. Manchester United sack Michael Carrick 10 days before Liverpool showdown

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick as head coach 10 days before their next fixture, which is against Liverpool at Anfield.

As was widely expected, the 45-year-old has paid the price for the Red Devils’ atrocious start to the season, with the Old Trafford outfit winning just one of their first 10 Premier League games and sitting in the relegation zone during the November international break.

Fabrizio Romano reported the news via X on Thursday morning, with other media outlets then confirming it before an official announcement from the club was communicated.

As per Sky Sports, Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be named as Carrick’s successor, with Man United having an agreement in place with the Argentine – currently in charge of the USA men’s national team – to take over after their CONCACAF Nations League in the coming week.

Should that impending appointment be completed in the anticipated timeframe, the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss would be in place in time for the Red Devils’ visit to Anfield on Sunday 22 November.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Although the practice of ‘new manager bounce’ isn’t exactly a scientific formula, a myriad of case studies – a few of which involve Man United – may have injected trepidation into Liverpool fans ahead of the grudge match in L4 on Sunday week.

Carrick himself took over a Red Devils team in turmoil last January and, in his first two games, oversaw wins over Manchester City and Arsenal, who ultimately finished second and first in the Premier League.

Eight years ago, after Jose Mourinho got the sack at Old Trafford following a comprehensive defeat at Anfield, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer triggered an immediate upturn in form which saw them pick up 25 points from a possible 27 in the top flight.

Managerial changes aside, Man United have an annoying habit of pulling out a result against Liverpool when it’s least expected. In January 2025, they were 14th in the table when they faced the table-topping Reds on Merseyside and came away with a 2-2 draw.

Iraola has already tasted defeat twice at Anfield this season (against Man City and Arsenal). Another on Sunday week would rankle the most of all, especially when our arch-rivals have been so abysmal over the past three months but conveniently trigger a change just in time for their visit to L4.
